notes: Step 1 parts were correct: 1 Uno, 1 breadboard, 6 LEDs, 6 x 220 ohm resistors, 13 jumper wires (6 blue signal, 1 GND to rail, 6 short black cathode-to-rail). No parts added or dropped.

Layout follows the circuit image: each resistor straddles the centre gap (top end in the f-j half, bottom end in the a-e half) in columns 7,10,13,16,19,22. The blue wire from the Uno goes to the resistor's bottom-half column. The resistor's top end shares a strip with the LED anode, so the resistor sits on the anode side as drawn. The LED cathode is in the next column (8,11,14,17,20,23) and a short black wire takes it to the ground rail.

The image has the breadboard's row letters reversed (j at the top). The catalogue's 't' bank (rows a-e) is the half nearest the Uno signal wires, and 'b' (rows f-j) is the half holding the LEDs. The ground rail along the top of the image is named 'tn'.
Pin mapping: Uno pin 7 -> LED1, 6 -> LED2, 5 -> LED3, 4 -> LED4, 3 -> LED5, 2 -> LED6. Ground goes from the Uno GND header pin next to AREF (GND.1) to the ground rail.

Exact breadboard rows and the rail column the GND wire lands in are read approximately from the image; the connectivity is what matters. Repeats are not used because the breadboard coordinates differ per copy.
